IV. Now the way of Reduction of an Ephemeris, from
one Meridian to another is briefly thus ; viz. if the tw,
places propoſed, lye both in the ſame longitude, and (4
are equally diſtant from the Grand Meridian ; viz. of the
Canary Iſlands there needs no Reduction : But if the Lon-
gitude of your place be either greater or leſſer than the Lon:
gitude of that place for which your Ephemerides was cal.
culated, then 'tis requiſite there be an Xquation of time,
made for the difference of Meridians.

V. To perform which, you muſt by ſome good Cata-
flogue ( or otherwiſe by ebſervation ) obtain the true Loy.
gitude of your place, ( which to do exaQtly I conceive
will be found a matter of difficulty } and compare it with

SECT. -L


what a Nativity is,


BY a Nativity we are to underſtand, that very mo-
ment of time that the Infant is delivered, or ſepa-


| nated from the Mothers Womb, and receives the Im-


preſſica of Air upon it's tender Body ; and not that point
of time wherein part of the Body appears, ( as ſome are
pleaſcd to Cavil at ) Cardan affirms that to be the mo-
ment, in which the Infant draws his firſt Breath, or moves
the Lungs : in ſhort, that very punCiilio of time, wherein
the Child is ſaid to be compleatly Born into the World, is
the moment of the Nativity, in which the Stars are ſaid to
nave Influence upon the tender Body of the Native; and
the Poſition of Heaven for that very inſtant is to be con-
lidered, as the Ground-work, and Foundation whereon to
Build an Atrological Judgement of the Future Actions, or
Fate of the Native in the World. But ſince the obtain-
ing of this true moment of time is ſo exceeding difficult


by reaſon of the uncertainty of Clocks, Dials, or Watches,,
or

or any other means, Aftrologers have found out ſever

To Conclude this Chapter,


Let thoſe that would Direct a Nativity this way, draw
their work into this following Method, v:z.

I. For the Aſcendant, Rule a Quarto or Folio page into
ix Columns, and in the firſt place the Aſpects of the Pro-
miflors, in the ſecond Column the Longitn2e in the Sigacs
wherein thoſe AſpeCts fall, in the third Column the Ov-
lique Aſcention of the Promiſſors, in the fourth Column


the R. A. of the DireCtion of the Sur ( produced by ſub-


ſtrating the R. A. of time from Noon in the Radix, from
the Oblique Aſcention of the Promiſſor, and 270d. &«.)
in the fifth Column place the Sjgne, deg. and min, corre-
ſpondent to the R, A. of the Direction of the Sun, whici
is termed the true Direction of the Sun, and inthe 6th and
laſt the years and dayes correſpondent, pointing out (kc
time of the Accident.
